raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From Chrysler Building, carry on to New York Public Library, about a 13-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"A few blocks back, you passed the Chrysler Building, where the architect William Van Alen secretly built a 200-foot spire inside the stairwell and hoisted it into place in just an hour and a half.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"It shot the tower to 1,046 feet, 117 higher than his rival's, and the reveal left H. Craig Severance furious.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Two marble lions keep watch over the steps up from Fifth Avenue, and the story goes they roar Depression.","source_id":"37a01d30-aea8-41e4-b816-8f91469ec2bf","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["bf44061a-7a42-48c5-b004-6f3a68e89f22"]},{"text":"The lions were designed by the cutters.","source_id":"37a01d30-aea8-41e4-b816-8f91469ec2bf","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Look up past them, and you're facing what many art historians call the finest Beaux Arts building in America.","source_id":"7a3df9b5-065b-4292-ae38-efd5da52f179","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Carrère and Hastings finished it in 1911 for more than nine million dollars, and when it was dedicated it was the largest marble structure ever raised in the United States.","source_id":"7a3df9b5-065b-4292-ae38-efd5da52f179","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["bf44061a-7a42-48c5-b004-6f3a68e89f22","fe574cc0-c973-44bb-ac9b-6bbc76062bb5","824c4e37-3c04-4b12-90a8-42c49fd87b7d"]},{"text":"For the front they borrowed from Paris — the twin palaces on the north side of the Place de la Concorde, the same French Renaissance style, a careful harmony of columns, pediments, and statuary.","source_id":"7a3df9b5-065b-4292-ae38-efd5da52f179","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"This was New York's gilded age, when architects trained in France came home with European ideals: gleaming white limestone instead of brownstone, ground floors lifted for grand staircase entrances, Corinthian columns and sculptured keystones everywhere.","source_id":"824c4e37-3c04-4b12-90a8-42c49fd87b7d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Officially it's the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building, the main branch of the New York Public Library, and it was named a National Historic Landmark in 1965.","source_id":"fe574cc0-c973-44bb-ac9b-6bbc76062bb5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Inside wait 8.7 million books and artifacts, along with one of the longest and most famous reading rooms in the world — the recently restored Rose Main Reading Room and its lavish coffered ceiling.","source_id":"fe574cc0-c973-44bb-ac9b-6bbc76062bb5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["bf44061a-7a42-48c5-b004-6f3a68e89f22"]},{"text":"Writers like Norman Mailer and Alfred Kazin worked under that ceiling, and it's still open to anyone who's working — surely the most glamorous coworking space on earth.","source_id":"fe574cc0-c973-44bb-ac9b-6bbc76062bb5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["bf44061a-7a42-48c5-b004-6f3a68e89f22"]},{"text":"Then there's the treasure in the Rare Book Division: a Gutenberg Bible printed around 1455, one of just 48 that survive from the roughly 180 that Johannes Gutenberg made after he invented the printing press around 1440.","source_id":"87524c83-10d7-4c1f-a2cd-18b24ab0cbde","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"When it arrived from Europe, the story goes, officials at the New York Customs House were made to remove their hats in honor of the holy book.","source_id":"87524c83-10d7-4c1f-a2cd-18b24ab0cbde","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The library's had quite a cinematic life, too.","source_id":"a7b922b7-ac90-460d-af47-95e551b63c4f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Ghostbusters opens right here in 1984, down in the haunted stacks, with those same marble lions and here.","source_id":"37dbbbed-89b0-4248-9d35-33f02f8a5cb6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"And it only got livelier — the liquor-fueled literary salons of the poet-communist John Reed in
